title: Name the practice snapshot by its content

blocks.text: The practice portfolio has passed milestone 1's reader. Every later run must now say *which* inputs it solved, in a way any worker can check on any day: by a digest of the snapshot's content. Two exports of the same content must get the same name, and any real change, however small, a new one.

The snapshot is the practice series' format: nested dictionaries keyed by year, region, program or project id, lists that carry their order (`years`, each `cost` profile, spent year by year), ints for money, and one float, `rate`.

rows: the float cut to `PLACES` (6) decimals by fixed formatting, `-0.0` as `0.0`; `ValueError` for NaN or infinity
the snapshot as bytes: every float through `fixed`, every list in its own order, keys sorted at every level, separators `","` and `":"` with no spaces, ASCII only, NaN refused
the SHA-256 of the bytes as 64 hex digits, the same in every process
write the canonical bytes to `<digest>.json` only if that file does not exist yet; return the digest
read `<key>.json`, re-hash it, raise `Edited` if the bytes no longer hash to `key`, else return the parsed JSON

blocks.text: The documented byte form is what `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False)` writes: the planning team pinned the digest of their test snapshot from it, and your digest must match theirs byte for byte. Dictionaries in another order are the same content; a reversed cost profile is not. About thirty-five lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
import tempfile

from snapshot import Edited, Store, canonical, digest

snap = {"years": [2031, 2032], "rate": 0.0375, "budget": {2031: 500, 2032: 450},
        "projects": {"P7": {"cost": [80], "must": False}}}
same = {"projects": {"P7": {"must": False, "cost": [80]}}, "budget": {2032: 450, 2031: 500},
        "rate": 0.03750000004, "years": [2031, 2032]}

print("canonical bytes:", canonical(snap))
print("digest:", digest(snap))
print("digest of reordered copy:", digest(same))

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as root:
    store = Store(root)
    key = store.put(snap)
    print("read back:", store.get(key))
    (store.root / f"{key}.json").write_bytes(canonical({**snap, "rate": 0.04}))
    try:
        store.get(key)
        print("edited file read: no error")
    except Edited as error:
        print("edited file read:", error)

cases.says: the same snapshot with every dictionary in another order has the same 64-digit digest; one changed cost or budget gives a new one
the store names a snapshot by its digest, keeps one file for content sent twice in another order, and reads the same content back
a rate of 0.0500000001 is the rate 0.05; a rate of 0.050001 is not
a cost profile is spent year by year, so reversing it is a different snapshot
a NaN rate has no canonical form and is refused with ValueError
the bytes are exactly the documented form, so the digest equals the one the planning team pinned
two fresh processes with different hash salts compute the same digest
a stored file edited in place is refused on read
putting the same content again does not rewrite its file, so an edit stays visible

origin.section: The Snapshot Is Named by the Hash of Its Canonical Content

concepts: a digest of the snapshot's canonical bytes that is stable under reordering, float noise and fresh processes, and a store that refuses an edited file
